blockers.message: the review record has no `## code.review` section, while roles were active at it

findings.evidence: - A plugin system for export formats, so that PDF, XLSX, XML and JSON exports can be added later by dropping a module in `src/export/plugins/`.
findings.recommendation: The Why is accountants copying invoices one by one into a spreadsheet; a single CSV route answers it. Drop the plugin system from What Changes, the "Exports go through a plugin registry" decision in design.md (whose only rejected alternative, "a single CSV function (not extensible)", is dismissed for an extensibility no requirement needs) and task 1.2. As it stands, task 1.2 is verified by `npm test -- registry` while no spec requirement describes the registry, so its done state has nothing to be checked against; and discovering modules from `src/export/plugins/` at start-up is an unverified assumption on how the TypeScript build ships those files. Add the plugin system in its own change when a second format is actually requested.
findings.title: A plugin system for formats nobody asked for

findings.evidence: The settings page SHALL let a user choose their preferred export format among the installed plugins.
findings.location: specs/invoice-export/spec.md#Requirement: Users choose their export format
findings.recommendation: Nothing in the Why asks for a format preference, and with CSV as the only format there is nothing to choose. Remove this requirement, the settings page item of What Changes, the sentence "A settings page stores each user's preferred format." in design.md and task 2.1. If it were kept, its scenario "WHEN a user picks CSV / THEN exports use CSV" cannot be told apart from no preference, since `GET /invoices.csv` is CSV whatever is stored; the plan does not say where the preference is stored (a new column or table, i.e. a migration); and the `user-interface` and `migration` domains would have to be ticked in proposal.md#Domains.
findings.title: A per-user export-format setting nobody asked for

findings.recommendation: The change adds `GET /invoices.csv?month=YYYY-MM`, which returns every invoice of a month with customer and total, and the spec has no scenario for a caller who is not authenticated or not an accountant. Tick `security` (and decide on `personal-data` for customer names) so that its expert reviews who may call the route, and add an unauthorized-caller scenario to "Invoices are exported as CSV".
findings.title: security left unticked for a route exposing invoices
